_comment: What this pack measured when it was last validated.
It is a record, not an input: the gates live in profile.json and are checked
by scripts/validate-pack.mjs. This is here so a later run can see whether a
number moved, and by how much, rather than only whether it still clears a
profileFoldDigest: see validate-pack output; changing it invalidates the built index

_note: Six of these numbers were already stale when the 2026-08-05 rebuild
remeasured them — median 1773 -> 1803, p90 6008 -> 6010, max 17786 ->
17790, rowShapedLines 1911 -> 1921, tableRowsRecovered 2103 -> 2098,
romanPoints 10 -> 9. Nothing in that rebuild touches the grammar, and
content/ and the built bundle report the same figures, so this is the
record catching up with a parse it had already been given.
The parser moved from Gutenberg's plain text to its HTML on 2026-07-30.
Every number here moved with it, and none of the movements is a loss:
topics 135 -> 114. The plain-text parser opened a topic wherever it took a
paradigm caption for a run-heading, so amō and amor were two topics and the
six irregular verbs were six. The HTML has real headings, so those runs sit
under the heading the book gave them. No section became unreachable —
`assigned` went up, not down.
sourceSections 371 -> 376. The old reader required section numbers to run
strictly +1 and lost §372-375 (prosody, dropped either way) plus §222A.
textChars are measured on the words: the inline emphasis markup is stripped
before counting (see core's plainText). The median rose because whole
table cells now arrive whole, where the plain text truncated them at the
column edge and left the remainder as a loose line.
rowShapedLines 2015 -> 1911 with tableRowsRecovered 2052 -> 2103: fewer
lines carrying more rows, which is the wrapped-cell bug being fixed. A
cell that used to wrap over three physical lines is now one row.
Three backfill runs took the syllabus from 1,088 tests to 1,722, and every
topic is at or above its size-scaled target. The gap the coverage report
was built to expose is closed.
The 2026-07-30 reparse regrouped the syllabus, so 27 topics' tests were
carried onto the topic that now covers their sections (see
scripts/remap-tests.mjs). Nothing was regenerated and nothing was thrown
away — hence max 26 -> 63 tests on a topic, which is six merged paradigm
topics' worth of drills under one heading. Only §313, which the old
parser had swallowed into Conditional Sentences, was newly generated.
keptRatioPct covers two of the three backfill runs. gen-stats.json is
written when a run finishes, and the middle run was stopped by hand before
it wrote anything, so roughly 270 shipped tests have no rejection-rate
data. C6 reads green on what it can see, not on everything.
Rebuilt on 2026-08-05, and this is the first record of a map that
scripts/build-lemmas.mjs actually produced. The old note here said the
file predated the builder and was run in --verify mode only; that is no
longer true, so the drift it documented is gone.
Three things moved at once:
formKeys 353,557 -> 491,398. --max-rank went from 12,000 to 20,000, which
is past the end of a 19,342-long frequency list: the map now holds every
lemma the list ranks. 429 of them the dictionary has no entry for and
legitimately miss. Built with --merge, which kept exactly one key the
join now drops — `post scriptum`, which the frequency list calls a noun
and the dictionary calls a phrase.
nounGenderPct 43.2 -> 99.2. genderOf used to read sense tags only, and
wiktextract writes a noun's gender on the headword row (tagged
`canonical`) far more often than on a sense. Reading both is the fix; the
ingest already stored the rows. This is why citations now print
`rex, rēgis (m)` where they printed `rex, rēgis`, and why
profile.citationsVersion went 3 -> 4 to catch saved cards up.
meanGlossChars 67 -> 72, from raising glossOf's sense cap 3 -> 6.
packResolvedPct is C5 answered from what the pack ships, which is what a
student meets and what CI can check; it was 98.4%. The --ref figures in
the questions block above did not move, because the dictionary did not.
The two dictionary files grew with the map — 291 -> 842 KB and 619 ->
1359 KB — and both are fetched on demand rather than precached, so what
the study loop costs on a plane is unchanged.
